description: Claude Code only (the skill is an orchestrator over assess-repo, assess-team, architecture-overview-report and ai-readiness-diagnostic-report, so it is not a self-contained SKILL.md for Pi). A plain-language request for the full assessment package on a single-repo workspace, tallyhub (a tiny Node/Express tally service; one test, a one-job CI workflow, no PR or review data, a fake API key in src/config.js and a canary token in .assessment/secrets.env), with no external system reachable. The prompt names the two output directories but no file names, so naming is the plugin's convention. It tells the run to build no Excel workbook (no template is shipped and the helper needs python3 with openpyxl) and to write the PowerPoint brief with the dependency-free OpenXML fallback. Only what the suite owns is checked, not the per-dimension findings (the assess-* evals do that): the file set and date-consistent names under docs/assessment/ and reports/<portco>/reports/; the six JSON sidecars plus the dated baseline file parse and the findings carry the canonical fields; the manifest's execution mode, coverage words and listed artifacts; the inventory row's HEAD and branch against the real .git; complete adversarial justifications; Scorecard scores equal to the justifications' final scores; the executive summary's layout (flaky), numeric-first scores with letters derived from the shared scale, Deep-Dive averages and the note that Scorecard and Deep-Dive need not match (flaky), Deep-Dive Overall against the run's own repo and team reports (flaky); the deck as a zip with presentation.xml and 8-12 text slides; the baseline gap and a 30-day action to capture it (flaky); missing PR/review governance carried into risk, roadmap and justifications; file:line refs that resolve (flaky); no artifact reported as built that was not (flaky); no secret value in any written file or in the deck's XML; and nothing written outside the two directories. Limits: the Excel workbook (template fidelity, helper validation, evidence copy) is not exercised; neither is the multi-repo and architecture-overview/Mermaid path, an external system, or the ignored-and-untracked state of secrets.env; assess-team sees a one-commit history; structure and consistency do not show that any analysis is correct. The baseline arm (no skill) is expected to measure the plugin's conventions (file names, sidecars, summary layout, score format, deck shape), not general ability.
prompt:
Produce the full executive assessment package for this repository (it has no external systems: no GitHub, Jira or other tracker is reachable): the repository assessment, the team assessment, the normalized findings and metrics data, an adversarial review of the scores, an executive summary in markdown, and a PowerPoint brief with the key findings. Cite file and line for findings, and do not print any secret value you come across, only that one is present.

This is a non-interactive run: ask no questions and choose the recommended option for anything unclear. The assessment configuration in .assessment/external-systems.yaml is complete. Keep the working files under docs/assessment/ and publish the executive package under the reports directory that configuration names. There is no Excel template and no PowerPoint template in this sandbox, and openpyxl and python-pptx are not installed: do not build an Excel workbook, say so in the limitations, and build the PowerPoint brief as a plain OpenXML .pptx zip. Do not render diagrams or use the network. Write only under docs/assessment/ and the reports directory; do not change any other file and do not commit.
